mechanism: Fenugreek seeds contain soluble fiber and compounds that lower blood glucose. When combined with Metformin, the blood sugar-lowering effects are additive, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia.
recommendation: Monitor blood glucose levels closely. Consider reducing Metformin dose if hypoglycemic symptoms occur. Patient should be counseled to recognize signs of low blood sugar.

evidence.note: Fenugreek seed extract demonstrated significant hypoglycemic activity in diabetic patients
Case reports of enhanced hypoglycemia when fenugreek combined with oral antidiabetic agents

mechanism: Curcumin in turmeric has antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties. Combined with warfarin, this significantly increases bleeding risk and INR values.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use or monitor INR more frequently. Patient should report any unusual bleeding or bruising immediately.

evidence.note: Curcumin demonstrated antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects in vitro and in vivo

mechanism: Ashwagandha may increase thyroid hormone production. When combined with levothyroxine, this can lead to hyperthyroidism symptoms.
recommendation: Monitor thyroid function tests (TSH, T3, T4) regularly. Adjust levothyroxine dose as needed. Watch for symptoms of hyperthyroidism.

evidence.source: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
evidence.note: Ashwagandha root extract significantly increased T3 and T4 levels in subclinical hypothyroid patients

mechanism: Ginger inhibits thromboxane synthetase, reducing platelet aggregation. Combined with aspirin's antiplatelet effects, bleeding risk increases.
recommendation: Use caution. Monitor for signs of bleeding, especially before surgery or dental procedures.

evidence.note: Ginger extract inhibited platelet aggregation in human subjects

mechanism: Garlic has antithrombotic properties and may potentiate the anticoagulant effect of warfarin.
recommendation: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements. If patient insists on garlic use, monitor INR more frequently.

evidence.note: Case report of increased INR when garlic supplement added to warfarin therapy

mechanism: Ginkgo inhibits platelet-activating factor and may enhance anticoagulant effects.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. If used together, monitor INR closely and watch for bleeding.

evidence.note: Case reports of spontaneous bleeding associated with ginkgo use

mechanism: Both insulin and fenugreek lower blood glucose, leading to potentially dangerous hypoglycemia.
recommendation: Monitor blood glucose very closely. Insulin dose may need reduction. Educate patient on hypoglycemia symptoms.

evidence.note: Fenugreek improved glycemic control in type 1 diabetes patients

mechanism: Ginseng may interfere with digoxin assays and potentially alter digoxin pharmacokinetics.
recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels and cardiac function. Consider alternative herbs.

evidence.note: Ginseng caused false elevation of digoxin immunoassay results

mechanism: Both clopidogrel and turmeric have antiplatelet effects, increasing bleeding tendency.
recommendation: Use with caution. Monitor for bleeding, especially gastrointestinal or unusual bruising.

evidence.note: Additive antiplatelet effects increase bleeding risk when antiplatelet drugs combined with herbs

mechanism: Garlic has modest blood pressure-lowering effects. Combined with ACE inhibitors, may cause hypotension.
recommendation: Monitor blood pressure regularly. Watch for dizziness or fainting. Dose adjustment may be needed.

evidence.note: Garlic preparations showed blood pressure lowering effects in hypertensive patients

mechanism: Ginger may have modest cholesterol-lowering effects, potentially enhancing statin effects.
recommendation: Generally safe combination. Monitor lipid panel and liver function as usual with statin therapy.

evidence.note: Ginger showed lipid-lowering effects in hyperlipidemic patients

mechanism: Both have gastroprotective properties. Turmeric has anti-inflammatory effects that may complement PPI therapy.
recommendation: Generally considered safe. May provide additional gastric protection.

evidence.note: Curcumin demonstrated gastroprotective effects in various models

mechanism: Ginkgo may interfere with calcium channel blocker effects or cause paradoxical blood pressure increase in some patients.
recommendation: Monitor blood pressure. Consider alternative herbs for cognitive support.

evidence.note: Ginkgo showed potential to alter blood pressure medication effects

mechanism: Both have analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties. May provide enhanced pain relief.
recommendation: Generally safe. May allow lower paracetamol doses. Still observe maximum daily paracetamol limits.

evidence.note: Curcumin demonstrated comparable efficacy to NSAIDs in some pain conditions
